title: Simplifying secure data access with Delegated OneLake Shortcuts (Preview)
summary: Fabric Updates Blog post introducing Delegated OneLake Shortcuts as a preview auth option layered on top of the shortcut model already documented in this KB. The new material is the formal delegated-identity connection method for OneLake-to-OneLake and cross-tenant shortcuts, and how it differs from External Data Sharing - not the base mechanics of shortcuts, which onelake-shortcuts.json already covers.
audience: Fabric platform owners and data governance teams designing large-audience or cross-tenant data distribution who need an alternative to per-user pass-through access on shared datasets.
why_it_matters: Solves a scaling and cross-tenant governance gap in the existing pass-through shortcut model: instead of provisioning every downstream consumer individually on the source, a data owner can delegate access through one configured identity and let business units manage their own users behind it.
takeaways: Delegated OneLake Shortcuts are a preview feature that adds an optional delegated-identity authentication mode to shortcut creation, alongside the existing default pass-through mode.
The delegated identity can be an organizational account, a service principal, or a workspace identity, and is configured once on the shortcut connection rather than per consumer.
Delegated shortcuts now explicitly support cross-tenant scenarios, letting one Fabric tenant shortcut to OneLake data in another tenant through a configured identity.

Delegated shortcuts are positioned as distinct from External Data Sharing: delegated shortcuts assume the consumer already has an identity in the producer's tenant, while External Data Sharing is for consumers with no identity there.

claims.text: Delegated OneLake Shortcuts, in preview at the time of this post, add a second shortcut authentication mode where access to the target flows through one configured connection identity instead of each individual signed-in user's identity.

The delegated identity attached to a shortcut can be an organizational account, a service principal, or a workspace identity, and choosing delegation is optional per shortcut; shortcuts default to pass-through authentication unless delegation is explicitly selected at creation time.

Delegated shortcuts let a central data owner constrain what the delegated identity itself can see via table- and column-level OneLake security, while the consuming business unit separately manages OneLake security for its own end users on top of that already-constrained view.

Delegated shortcuts now support cross-tenant sharing: a Fabric tenant can create a shortcut to OneLake data that lives in a different organization's Fabric tenant, authenticating with an identity from that other tenant so downstream users access it through the configured delegated identity rather than needing individual cross-tenant permissions.

Cross-tenant delegated shortcuts are distinguished from Fabric's separate External Data Sharing feature: External Data Sharing targets consumers with no identity in the producer's tenant (e.g. an outside partner or an ISV's customers), while cross-tenant delegated shortcuts assume the consumer already holds an identity, such as an organizational account or service principal, in the producer's tenant.

A named use case for cross-tenant delegated shortcuts is sharing curated data between an organization's own test and production tenants, or between a parent company and a subsidiary, using the same zero-copy, intersection-based security model that applies to delegated shortcuts within a single tenant.

Switching an existing shortcut between pass-through and delegated authentication is not an in-place setting change: the documented procedure is to delete the shortcut and recreate it with the desired authentication method.

Creating a delegated shortcut in the Fabric portal is done from Get data > New table shortcut, choosing Microsoft OneLake as the source, then selecting Delegated identity as the connection method and either reusing or creating a connection with an organizational-account or service-principal authentication kind.
